american_samoa_no_district.description: American Samoa (5 county-equivalents, GEOIDs 60010-60050) belongs to no federal judicial district; county_district.csv carries it with district_id ''. It is not drawn.
american_samoa_no_district.reason: American Samoa is not part of any judicial district: no section of 28 U.S.C. §§ 81-131 or of title 48 creates a federal district court for it (its trial court is the territorial High Court).

cb2025_20m_lacks_island_areas.description: The 1:20m Census county file omits AS, GU, MP, VI; it is not used for geometry (the low-res topology is simplified from the 1:500k file instead).

hawaii_outlying_islands_not_drawn.description: 28 U.S.C. § 91 includes in the District of Hawaii: Midway Islands, Wake Island, Johnston Island, Sand Island, Kingman Reef, Palmyra Island, Baker Island, Howland Island, Jarvis Island, Canton Island, Enderbury Island. None is a Census county-equivalent, so none is drawn or listed in county_district.csv.
hawaii_outlying_islands_not_drawn.reason: Not present in Census county files (cb_2025/tl_2025 contain no U.S. Minor Outlying Islands); Canton and Enderbury are no longer U.S. territory.

legacy_files_unavailable.description: Historical county files that www2.census.gov answered with a 'Request Rejected' page (HTTP 200) on every attempt: https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/PREVGENZ/co/co00shp/co19_d00_shp.zip. Legacy GEOIDs that appear only in these files are missing from legacy_geoids.csv.
legacy_files_unavailable.reason: Census CDN/WAF rejection; not worked around.

ny_concurrent_waters_not_drawn.description: 28 U.S.C. § 112(b)-(c): S.D.N.Y. and E.D.N.Y. share jurisdiction over certain waters. Shared jurisdiction is not drawable as territory; maps show the county lists only.

split_counties_whole_in_county_tables.description: Eight counties are divided by a statutory carve-out: Park and Gallatin MT and Fremont ID (Yellowstone NP -> wyd, 28 U.S.C. §§ 92, 106, 131); Hoke, Moore, Scotland and Richmond NC (Fort Bragg / Camp MacKall -> nced) and Durham NC (FCI Butner -> nced), § 113(a)-(b). The district polygons are cut, but each county's row in county_district.csv (and its feature in the hi TopoJSON `counties` object) carries one district_id: the district holding the rest of the county (mtd, idd or ncmd). Any county->district sum, such as a Census population denominator or the county_equivalents count, therefore credits the carved-out parts to mtd, idd and ncmd instead of wyd and nced. The largest share is Hoke County, NC: 362.3 of 1,014.3 km² (36%) is in nced (split_counties.csv). These rows carry split_districts and split_note; no sub-county population split is produced by this lane, so per-capita rates for these five districts that use a county-sum denominator are approximate.
split_counties_whole_in_county_tables.reason: Census county rows are indivisible here; allocating the carved parts' population would need block-level counts (population lane), and area shares are not population shares.

statutory_places_not_named_gud_vid.description: Title 48 names no place of holding court for the District Court of Guam or the District Court of the Virgin Islands; statute_places.csv has no rows for gud and vid.

tennessee_river_waters_not_delineated.description: 28 U.S.C. § 123(c)(1): W.D. Tenn. (Eastern Division) includes the waters of the Tennessee River to the low-water mark on the eastern shore where the river divides the Western and Middle Districts. That strip is not drawn; the Census county lines are used as is.
tennessee_river_waters_not_delineated.reason: No allowed public source gives the historical low-water line of the (now impounded) river.
